item.research_question: How do individual deformation mechanisms compete or synergize during plastic deformation in high-entropy alloys at ultralow temperatures, and what is the specific deformation pathway activated?
item.processing_route: Arc melting of pure elements (>99.9% purity) in Ti-gettered argon, remelted 8 times, drop-cast into Cu molds, homogenized at 1200°C for 24 hours, cold rolled to ~80% reduction, recrystallized at 800°C for 1 hour, and quenched in iced water to achieve ~5 μm grain size; tensile specimens prepared by electrical discharge machining.
item.test_conditions: In situ neutron diffraction under tensile loading at 15 K, 140 K, and room temperature; strain rate of 2.67 × 10−5 s−1 (0.04 mm/min) in the plastic regime; vacuum ~10−5 kPa.
key_findings: At 15 K, the alloy exhibited an extraordinarily high strength of ~2.5 GPa combined with ~62% ductility.
Serrated deformation characterized by sharp load drops began beyond 21% strain, with amplitudes approaching 570 MPa near the ultimate tensile strength.
Stacking fault probability (SFP) developed early at stress > 1075 MPa and increased to 27 × 10−3 before fracture, whereas SFP was almost zero at room temperature.
The deformation pathway at 15 K followed a sequence: dislocation slip (yielding at ~718 MPa) → stacking faults (at ~1075 MPa) → twinning and serrations (at ~1270 MPa).
The (220)//LD diffraction peak disappeared almost entirely toward the end of deformation, indicating significant texture development.
The strain-hardening rate at 15 K was stable until fracture, unlike at 295 K where it decreased with deformation.
Fracture occurred via two shear bands at ~90° angles with no significant necking, despite 62% true strain.
item.mechanism: The extreme work hardening and large ductility result from the cooperation of multiple deformation mechanisms: dislocation slip initiates deformation, followed by stacking faults and twinning which create additional boundaries that impede dislocation propagation. Stacking faults act as a critical bridge preventing a direct transition to serration-induced failure. The low stacking fault energy and the stability of the face-centered cubic structure at ultralow temperatures, enabled by high-entropy alloying, facilitate this pathway. Local disorder from the multicomponent nature prevents the propagation of serration flow, allowing continued strengthening until major shear bands form.
item.limitations: The thermocouples were located at the sample grips rather than on the sample gauge section, meaning there could be a delay in temperature sensing and the local temperature rise in the deformed region could be much higher than measured.
item.future_work: The authors suggest that insights from in situ experiments point to the role of entropy in the design of structural materials with superior properties, specifically utilizing the unique combination of complex chemistry and simple crystal structure to deploy competitive mechanisms in synergy.
quotes: The coexistence of multiple deformation pathways raises an important question regarding how individual deformation mechanisms compete or synergize during plastic deformation.
Quantitative analysis showed that the cooperation of these different deformation mechanisms led to extreme work hardening.
The intermediate step, SF, is critically important and highlights the influence of entropy and lattice instability on deformation and mechanical behaviors.
